column3: BootUI says "Enable content type sniffing protection through Spring Security headers or equivalent middleware." sharpit names security-header middleware.
BootUI links to https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/web/servlet.html. sharpit links to FastAPI's error-handling guide.
BootUI links to https://owasp.org/Top10/2025/A10_2025-Mishandling_of_Exceptional_Conditions/. sharpit replaces its previous Spring Boot servlet link with FastAPI's error-handling guide.
BootUI says "Spring MVC mappings have not been inspected yet." sharpit refers to the application's routes.
BootUI says "Security headers, cookies, CORS, errors, and actuator mappings have not been inspected yet." sharpit refers to route exposure.
BootUI says "BootUI does not send injection payloads. Use a dedicated scanner and manual review." sharpit substitutes its own name.
BootUI says "BootUI cannot infer the host application's threat model or business logic design." sharpit substitutes its own name.
BootUI says "Spring Security wiring has not been inspected yet." sharpit checks synthetic response headers for HTTP Basic or Digest challenges.
BootUI says "Deserialization and serialization-filter posture have not been inspected yet." sharpit refers to deserialization safeguards.
sharpit's ASGI limitation has no verbatim BootUI counterpart. The note states the limits of static route and middleware evidence.
BootUI says "Spring Security wiring, handler mappings, and SecurityFilterChain CSRF posture were inspected for authorization review prompts." sharpit's scan does not assess route authorization.

BootUI uses "No findings were produced by the evaluated synthetic-response, Spring configuration, and Spring MVC mapping checks. This does not establish that every route, authorization rule, or deployment edge is configured safely." sharpit's review note names the retained responses and synthetic CORS preflight and states the limits of that evidence.

BootUI uses "No findings were produced by the evaluated synthetic-response, Spring configuration, and Spring MVC mapping checks. This does not establish that every route, authorization rule, or deployment edge is configured safely." sharpit's no-finding note refers to the synthetic GET and CORS preflight and states the limits of that evidence.

BootUI says "No findings were produced by the evaluated Spring authentication metadata. Endpoint authentication, account policy, and runtime login behavior were not tested." sharpit states whether Basic or Digest response headers produced a review finding and explains that dependency-based authentication is outside the scan.

BootUI says "No findings were produced by the evaluated Jackson default-typing and JVM ObjectInputFilter checks. Custom deserializers, update integrity, and trusted artifact boundaries still require manual review." sharpit's local scan does not assess deserialization safeguards.
